how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

sentences.ar: أربع containers، وبتختار بينهم بالعملية اللي بتعملها أكتر، مش بالعادة.
sentences.en: Four containers, and you choose between them by the operation you do most, not by habit.
A dictionary maps a key to a value.

sentences.ar: الـset بتفرض uniqueness. والـtuple record ثابت.
sentences.en: A set enforces uniqueness. A tuple is a fixed record.

sentences.ar: وأهو اللي بيضيّع وقت الناس فعلاً: إنك تشوف حاجة موجودة في list ولا لأ معناه إنك تلف على الـlist كلها عشر آلاف مقارنة لعشر آلاف عنصر.
sentences.en: Here is the one that costs people real time: checking whether something is in a list means walking the list — ten thousand comparisons for ten thousand items.

sentences.ar: نفس الفحص على set بيبقى خطوة واحدة في المتوسط، لأن الـset بتعمل hash للقيمة وتوصل لمكانها على طول.
sentences.en: The same check against a set is one hop, on average, because a set hashes the value straight to its location.

sentences.ar: حطّ الفحص ده جوه loop على عشر آلاف صف تانيين، وتبقى بنيت بإيدك الفرق بين تانيتين وخمس دقايق.
sentences.en: Put that check inside a loop over another ten thousand rows and you have just built the difference between two seconds and five minutes.

sentences.ar: بعدها: الداتا بتختفي لما البرنامج يقف، إلا لو كتبتها في مكان.
sentences.en: Next: data disappears when the program stops, unless you write it somewhere.

sentences.ar: الـCSV صفوف وأعمدة، مسطّحة وموجودة في كل حتة.
sentences.en: CSV is rows and columns, flat and everywhere.

sentences.ar: والـJSON بيحافظ على الـnesting، وعشان كده الـAPIs بتتكلم بيه.
sentences.en: JSON keeps nesting, which is why APIs speak it.

sentences.ar: وأخيراً الـenvironments أقل فكرة جذابة وأكترهم تحميل.
sentences.en: And finally, environments — the least glamorous and most load-bearing idea here.

sentences.ar: الـvirtual environment بيبعد dependencies المشروع ده عن أي مشروع تاني.
sentences.en: A virtual environment keeps this project's dependencies away from every other project's.

sentences.ar: والـrequirements.txt بيسجّل بالظبط إنت نزّلت إيه.
sentences.en: A requirements.txt records exactly what you installed.

sentences.ar: من غير الاتنين، جملة "شغال عندي على جهازي" مش نكتة، دي bug report مش قادر تعمل بيها حاجة.
sentences.en: Without both, the sentence "it works on my machine" is not a joke, it is a bug report you cannot act on.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.

concepts.def_en: An ordered, changeable Python collection that allows duplicates and index access; checkin…

concepts.failure: Forgetting the trailing comma, so a one-element tuple is just the bare value.

concepts.def_en: A construct that repeats a block of code for each item or until a condition changes.
concepts.failure: Off-by-one bounds, or a condition that never changes, looping forever.

concepts.def_en: Comma-separated values: a plain-text format of flat rows and columns, simple and universal but with no types or nesting.

concepts.def_en: A text format for nested key-value and list data, the common language of APIs.
concepts.def_ar: format نصي للداتا المتداخلة (key-value وlists)، وهو اللغة المشتركة للـAPIs.
concepts.failure: Assuming JSON keeps Python types like tuples or dates after a round trip.

concepts.failure: Changing a response field or meaning without versioning, breaking every client that depen…

concepts.def_en: Interfaces through which programs call each other to request data or actions, typically o…
concepts.failure: Calling an API without handling errors, timeouts or rate limits.

concepts.def_en: An isolated Python environment holding one project's own libraries and versions, so projects never conflict with each other.

concepts.failure: Installing packages globally, or forgetting to activate the environment before running the project.
